name: HUNGARY
lead: Hungary is in the middle of Europe, ringed by the Carpathian mountains. Budapest is two cities joined by bridges over the Danube. Hungarians invented the Rubik's Cube, the ballpoint pen and the noiseless safety match. Over 1,300 hot springs bubble up underground.
geo: Hungary is almost flat, like a giant bowl. The Puszta, or Great Plain, is a windy grassland where cowboys once rode. The Danube and Tisza rivers cut the land into thirds.
Lake Balaton is Central Europe's largest lake. Its warm, shallow water draws millions of swimmers and sailors every summer.
animals: On the Puszta live grey cattle and racka sheep with corkscrew horns. The great bustard, the world's heaviest flying bird, still strides across the plains.
Giant catfish and sturgeon swim in the Danube. White-tailed eagles, with wings as wide as a sofa, patrol the riverbanks.
culture: Hungarian food is painted red with paprika. Goulash (gulyás) began as a herdsman's campfire soup on the Puszta and is now loved around the world.
Béla Bartók recorded old folk songs in villages on wax cylinders. On Sunday mornings, families soak in 36°C mineral pools.
history: Magyar tribes galloped in from the Ural steppes and settled here in AD 895. King Stephen I received a crown from the Pope around 1000 AD.
Ottomans ruled Hungary for 150 years, then Habsburgs for nearly two centuries. In 1989 Hungarians peacefully took down the Iron Curtain fence.
wows: Ernő Rubik's 1974 cube is the best-selling puzzle toy ever.
Budapest's metro Line 1 (1896) was the first on the European continent.
Hungary wins more Olympic golds per person than almost any country.
Laszlo Biro patented the ballpoint pen in 1938.
Lake Balaton averages just 3 m deep.
Budapest has over 100 thermal springs, more than any other capital.

myths.myth: Paprika is always hot and spicy
myths.fact: Most paprika is sweet and mild. Only some types are hot.

myths.myth: The Rubik's Cube was made as a toy
myths.fact: Rubik built it to teach students about 3D shapes. It took him a month to solve his own cube.
